output.data:
Is this gene patterned, or are its cells?

Spatially variable gene tests rank genes by how clumped their expression is on the tissue. But cell types clump too. If a gene is made only by enterocytes, and enterocytes line the villus tips, the gene will look patterned even if every enterocyte expresses it the same way. Most of a top list can be cell layout in disguise.
One test, three inputs Yan, Hua & Li (2025) sort spatially variable genes into kinds, including overall and cell-type-specific. You don't need a different method for each kind. You need one test, fed three different things.
We use one mouse ileum slice from Xu et al. (2026) (MERFISH, 30,332 cells). All-cell and leftover scores use the 390 genes detected in at least 1% of all cells. Within a cell type, the floor is 1% of the cells in that selection. The pooled enterocytes clear 243 genes. The test is Moran's I (Moran 1950, via Squidpy). It asks whether neighboring cells have similar expression. Think of a seating chart. Moran's I is high when people who sit together wear the same color. We ask it three ways:
  1. All cells. Is the gene patterned anywhere?
  2. Leftover expression. Remove what each cell's own type and its spatial domain predict, then test what's left. The 22 spatial domains are Squidpy neighborhood clusters on cell type, the same call as the niche recipe, labelled spatial domain. Positional labels such as Enterocyte (bottom), (mid), and (top) stay as Xu annotated them. Using domain as a covariate follows Liu & Li (2026).
  3. One cell type. Select the cell type in the widget before coloring a cell-type-specific gene. That selection is the context.
Enterocyte subtypes are positions Xu et al. split enterocytes into bottom, mid and top by where they sit along the villus, not by an independent marker. Those labels already carry the villus gradient. When the leftover score regresses out cell type, it also regresses out position, so zonated genes like Apob lose most of their score by construction rather than because they lack a pattern. The same goes for testing within "Enterocyte (top)" alone: that slice covers only a thin band of the villus, so a gradient has little room to show. To see zonation, select all three enterocyte subtypes together, then color Apob.
Reading the scores A gene that scores high in 1 but drops to zero in 2 is cell layout. A gene that stays high in 2 or 3 has spatial biology of its own.
Try it Select the cell type in the widget first when the gene belongs to one kind of cell, then color the gene. Acta2 is cell layout. On all cells it is rank 1 (I = 0.74). Leftover I is 0.01, and inside enterocytes it is 0.03. Apob is a villus gradient inside enterocytes. Select the enterocyte positions, then color Apob. Within those cells, pooled without merging the bottom, mid, and top labels, I = 0.52. Expression rises toward the villus tip (Spearman 0.71 with mucosal_pseudospace, mean 0.65 in the bottom fifth and 5.29 in the top fifth). In enterocytes, Apob mRNA increases toward the villus tip as part of the upper-villus chylomicron program; Nt5e/Cd73 marks the sharper extreme-tip program (Moor et al. 2018, Beumer et al. 2022, Manco et al. 2021, Xu et al. 2026). Dhx58 is patchy beyond cell makeup. It moves from rank 59 on all cells to rank 2 on leftover expression. It is not zonated (Spearman -0.00 with mucosal_pseudospace). Zonation trio in enterocytes. Apob rises toward the tip. Nt5e (Cd73) switches on at the extreme tip (mean 0.00 in the bottom fifth, 0.30 in the top fifth, Spearman 0.21). Cps1 falls toward the tip (mean 3.62 to 0.17, Spearman -0.57). Il22ra2 is the rare marker the floor is for. It is detected in 42 cells, under 1% of all cells, so all-cell and leftover scores do not rank it. It is detected in 2 pooled enterocytes, under 1% of those cells, so the within-enterocyte score does not rank it either. All-cell I is 0.15. Leftover I, after own type and spatial domain, is 0.02.
Caveat Moran's I sees one scale, set by 6 neighbors, and rare cell types give small, noisy subsets. When you need a proper statistical test, use a dedicated method like nnSVG or SPARK.
